relevance_note: Describes LCAT-D homozygotes and their relatives individually (e.g. 'none of the four homozygotes for LCAT-D had detectable Lp(a) in their plasma'), though no LCAT variant is printed.
method_note: Read the whole paper; a Python script assembled the JSON from values I chose by reading, and sliced Table I row prefixes for spans (each checked against the table by eye and by assert). No LCAT variant (cDNA/protein) is printed anywhere; variant rows keep variant_original_string 'not reported' and carry only zygosity as stated (homozygous LCAT-D per the Table I legend / text; J.M. and I.S. called heterozygotes). Table I is mangled in conversion: the W family block has data columns headed 'W family - 1' to 'W family - 11' (bare numbers 1-11, labelled 'Table I #n'; * = homozygous: #2, #9, #10); the S family block has columns J.M. (data col 2), G.S.* (col 4), I.S. (col 6), S.S. (col 8), Normal values (col 10). All 11 W family members and 4 S family members are included as relatives described in Table I; W heterozygotes cannot be identified (pedigree Fig. 1 not available), so W non-homozygotes have no variant rows. Seven Norwegian homozygotes (refs 43, 44) are included because the paper gives an individual fact (Lp(a) not detectable). Labels: 'I.S.' occurs in the S family and Norwegian family 1, and 'L.G.' in Norwegian families 2 and 3, so these carry '(Family n)'; 'R.M' is as printed (no final period). 'Proband' is used in this paper for any study subject (even a normolipemic donor), so is_proband is left null. Clinical features (corneal opacities, hemolytic anemia, glomerulosclerosis), low HDL-C/apoA-I/apoD, elevated apoE, LpX and undetectable Lp(a) come from statements about 'The LCAT-D patients' / 'all four affected persons' / 'the four homozygotes' of the two Austrian families and are recorded as inferred from group statement for W #2, #9, #10 and G.S. Table I numbers (e.g. HDL-C, FC/TC) were not interpreted against the printed normal values on their own; so 'reduced cholesteryl ester fraction' and 'elevated unesterified cholesterol' are not reported for the W homozygotes despite FC/TC 0.88-0.99, and low HDL-C is not recorded for relatives with HDL-C below 35. G.S. kidney transplantation is inferred from 'kidney transplantation in one individual within each family' plus the S family having a single LCAT-D patient; the W family transplant recipient is not identifiable. Renal failure is not stated for anyone, so that checklist item is not reported. Hypertriglyceridemia for J.M. and I.S. is from 'indicated elevated VLDL-TG concentrations'. Contradictions/oddities: the Introduction says nine heterozygotes had Lp(a) 2-13 mg/dl, but the Discussion says J.M., an obligatory heterozygote, lacked Lp(a); Table I normal TG is printed '>150' (probably a conversion error for '<150'); 'nmol/mI' typo in the S family LCAT row. Excluded Lp(a)-deficiency rows for unaffected members (Lp(a) 2-13 mg/dl group statement) were not created.
